# DevRites

> DevRites turns Claude Code into a disciplined senior engineer: it specs a feature, plans it, builds one verified slice at a time, proves the work with on-disk evidence, reviews it with fresh-context agents, and refuses to claim "done" without proof. Free and open source (MIT).

DevRites is a project-local pack of Claude Code skills (slash commands like /rite-spec, /rite-build, /rite-seal) plus engineering rules, review subagents, a tool-agnostic CLI, and an MCP server. Feature state lives on disk under .devrites/work/<slug>/ as Markdown, so a fresh agent resumes exactly where the last one stopped. A Spec Drift Guard halts the build when the plan is revealed wrong; type-GO requires a typed confirmation before any irreversible git operation; AFK mode runs unattended but never silently accepts destructive migrations, auth changes, public-API breaks, or red tests.

## Lifecycle

The ten-phase feature lifecycle, each phase reading the last one's files and writing its own:

- spec (/rite-spec): investigate the codebase, write spec.md with measurable acceptance criteria
- temper (/rite-temper): strategic review and pre-mortem of the spec before planning
- define (/rite-define): decompose the spec into a plan and vertical task slices
- vet (/rite-vet): engineering review of the plan, writes the test plan the build must satisfy
- build (/rite-build): implement exactly one verified slice, test-first, then stop with evidence
- prove (/rite-prove): full tests, build, types, lint, and browser proof against acceptance criteria
- polish (/rite-polish): behavior-preserving cleanup, then UI polish against the design system
- review (/rite-review): parallel fresh-context reviewers check the diff against spec and standards
- seal (/rite-seal): GO / NO-GO decision gate over the evidence
- ship (/rite-ship): the gated, irreversible commit/push/tag, then archive the workspace

## Tool-agnostic core

- The `devrites` CLI exposes deterministic gates where the exit code is the verdict: `orient`, `ready`, `evidence-fresh`, `acceptance`, `active`, `list`, `use`, `resolve`.
- A dependency-free MCP stdio server exposes the same operations as tools (devrites_ready, devrites_acceptance, devrites_orient, ...). Register it in a project's .mcp.json.
- The same files and gates are drivable from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, a CI job, or a human.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://devrites.com/docs/): quick start, the on-disk workspace, where to go next
- [Command map](https://devrites.com/docs/command-map.html): every command and skill, what it reads and writes
- [Flow](https://devrites.com/docs/flow.html): the lifecycle, the Spec Drift Guard loop, and the two run modes
- [Architecture](https://devrites.com/docs/architecture.html): the layers, the naming convention, and the design rationale

## Install

- Install into a project: `curl -fsSL https://devrites.com | bash`
- Update: `curl -fsSL https://devrites.com/update | bash`
- Uninstall: `curl -fsSL https://devrites.com/remove | bash`
- DevRites is project-local and never writes to ~/.claude.
